briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for July 25, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Global Climate Crisis and Extreme Weather Phenomena
sections.content: Globally, extreme weather phenomena are intensifying alongside the acceleration of climate change [26]. In the United States, severe and widespread heatwaves are occurring, making the reality of climate change palpable [21, 22], and across Europe, climate change is triggering drought risks and fine dust pollution events [36, 37]. Notably, large-scale wildfires in Spain and southern France have led to the evacuation or lockdown of over 200,000 people [44, 45, 46], and tree-ring analysis has revealed the history of droughts, wildfires, and climate change [38]. Furthermore, the world is currently witnessing one of the fastest intensifying El Niño phenomena, which increases the likelihood of record-high temperatures in 2026 [50].

sections.title: ⚠️ Domestic Climate Policies and Discussions on Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: Domestically, active discussions are ongoing regarding renewable energy transition policies. The Climate Minister warned that an over-reliance on renewable energy alone could lead to increased electricity bills and price surges, stating that renewable energy alone is insufficient as an alternative to coal [8, 10, 11, 18]. Conversely, Representative Han Jeoung-ae emphasized water energy as a key resource for stabilizing the power grid in the era of renewable energy [15], and it was also argued that cross-transmission and the activation of hydrothermal energy would be key to achieving 100GW of renewable energy [9]. Mr. Kim Yong-beom announced a 'National Energy Vision' in August, foreshadowing a comprehensive overhaul of renewable energy and grid infrastructure [13], and various policy approaches are being explored, including expanded support for solar panel installation in water source protection areas and the proposal of an 'Inje-type Renewable Energy Pension' [16, 17].

sections.title: 🌱 Expansion of Climate Action and Adaptation Efforts
sections.content: Domestic and international efforts are being deployed in various ways to respond to climate change and achieve carbon neutrality. Domestically, Namwon City has completed the maintenance of its sewage facilities in preparation for increasingly frequent heavy rainfall due to climate change [1], and the Korea Rural Community Corporation has strengthened international cooperation by concluding training to enhance Guatemala's climate change response capabilities [2]. The Taean Haean National Park Office and the Blue Carbon Project Group signed a business agreement for carbon neutrality [4], and the Mayor of Daejeon met with the EU Ambassador to Korea to discuss expanding cooperation in advanced industries and carbon neutrality [5]. Furthermore, Baebang-eup in Asan is promoting the reduction of single-use items with local daycare centers [6], and Sacheon City is conducting pilot projects for carbon neutrality practices targeting rural women leaders and children, thereby promoting the spread of carbon neutrality in daily life [7]. Internationally, the participation of the financial sector is also expanding, with BBVA issuing $30 million worth of sustainability bonds for climate change action [33].

sections.title: 🌍 Widespread Socio-economic Impacts of Climate Change
sections.content: Climate change is having diverse impacts across society, extending beyond mere weather phenomena. UN agencies have warned that conflict and climate change threaten progress in combating global hunger [24], and in the United States, an analysis found that people with disabilities are more likely to report health harms from global warming [23]. São Toméans feel their lives are worsening due to climate change and support climate adaptation and resilience policies [28]. Meanwhile, unexpected changes are also being observed, such as climate change enabling the cultivation of tropical fruits in Florida [31], and scientists have even stated that climate change is slowly lengthening Earth's day [32]. In this situation, the understanding that recycling alone cannot stop climate change is spreading [35], and insurance companies are seriously recognizing the risks of climate change [25].

briefing.closing: The climate-related news gathered today demonstrates that various policy discussions and practical efforts are being pursued concurrently, both domestically and internationally, amidst a global crisis. Continuous attention and response to the widespread impacts of climate change are necessary. This concludes today's climate briefing.
